To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we give two graphical assumptions which are necessary and sufficient for the identification of the latent structure of a linear model with non-Gaussian or heterogenous error terms.

(1) the two conditions are both necessary and sufficient for the identifiability of the causal structure of the latent variables; (2) the first of the two conditions can be relaxed to a weaker condition that is still sufficient; (3) the two conditions can also be applied to partially observed heterogeneous linear models; (4) our conditions can be satisfied for a large number of hidden variables, even when the observed variables are only a small subset of the latent variables.

the two graphical conditions, together with one condition on the coefficients of the model, are necessary and sufficient for the identifiability of partially observed linear non-Gaussian and heterogeneous models, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of causal models with latent variables.

the problem of identifying the causal structure in partially observed linear models, and we provide two graphical conditions that are necessary and sufficient for the identifiability of the causal structure in this case.
the problem of identifying the causal structure among latent variables.

, in a partially observed linear non-Gaussian model, the causal structure of the latent variables is identified by the following conditions: (i) there exists no latent variable which is a direct descendant of all the observed variables; (ii) the graph of the latent variables has no directed cycles; and (iii) the coefficients are generic
, if there are more latent variables than observed variables, then the causal structure of the observed variables cannot be identified, even if the errors are non-Gaussian and heterogeneous.
, if the two conditions hold for a partially observed linear model, the causal structure of the model is identifiable, provided that the coefficients of the causal edges satisfy a generic condition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we give graphical conditions that are sufficient for the identifiability of partially observed linear causal models with either non-gaussian or heterogeneous errors, and that these conditions can be satisfied in many practical situations.
we provide a set of necessary and sufficient conditions for the identification of partially observed linear causal models with either non- Gaussian or heterogeneous errors.
we have provided a necessary and sufficient graphical condition for identifiability of the causal structure in the partially observed linear model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the causal structure among latent variables can be identified even when the latent variables themselves are causally related, as long as the number of causal edges is sufficiently low.
in the presence of latent variables, the sparsity of the graph of causal relations is a key condition for identifiability.
the identification of the latent causal structure is possible even when the observed variables are generated by a large number of confounders or mediators.
